methods.label: Use volume, then construct the subdivision
methods.explanation:
Each smaller cube must have edge length \(1\) or \(2\) cm. Since the pieces are not all the same size, both sizes must occur.

Let \(k\) be the number of cubes with edge \(2\) cm. The original cube has volume \(3^3=27\) cubic centimeters, and each edge-2 cube has volume \(2^3=8\) cubic centimeters. The remaining volume therefore consists of \(27-8k\) unit cubes, so the total number of pieces is
\[
N=k+(27-8k)=27-7k.
\]
There is at least one edge-2 cube and at least one unit cube, so \(k\geq1\) and \(8k<27\). Thus \(k\) must be \(1\), \(2\), or \(3\), giving the necessary candidate counts \(20\), \(13\), or \(6\). Only \(20\) appears among the choices.

To verify that \(20\) is achievable, imagine the original cube divided into \(27\) unit cells. Leave a \(2\times2\times2\) block at one corner as one uncut cube, and cut the rest into unit cubes. The block occupies \(8\) cells, leaving \(27-8=19\) unit cubes. This gives \(1+19=20\) pieces of two different sizes. Therefore the answer is \(\boxed{20}\), choice E.
